newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Mobile phone companies sag.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Mobile phone companies sag.

text.p: European mobile phone companies sagged on Wednesday to highlight quiet trading in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Traders said most ADRs had followed the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq slightly lower.
"We've had a strong last couple of days and the market feels a little top heavy," a trader said.
Mobile phone companies fell in light to moderate trade as they consolidated recent strong rises.
Sweden's LM Ericsson, which was at 28-1/2 in mid-December, was off 5/8 to 34-1/2. Finland's Nokia Group fell 1-1/4 to 63-3/8.
Britain's Vodafone Group fell 1-1/2 to 45-1/4 and France's Alcatel Alsthom Cie Generale d'Electricite' dropped 5/8 to 21-5/8.

The French government set terms for the sale of its Thomson-CSF military electronics company and ruled out state defense company Aerospatiale as a sole or joint bidder. Alcatel Alsthom had allied itself with Aerospatiale and plane maker Dassault to bid for Thomson-CSF.
Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel fell 2-1/4 to 72-5/8 after German sector rival Hoechst AG plunged on plans not to list a subsidiary publicly and issued a weak sales outlook for 1997.
Among Latin American shares, Brazilian telephone company Telebras fell 1-1/8 to 107-7/8.
Decliners led advancers by 293 to 167 among 806 ADRs, and ADRs showed a 0.67 percent decline. Volume was 25 million shares at midday.
